subject: social-studies

grade_and_subject.standards_system_name: Florida's State Academic Standards – Social Studies

domains.domain_name: Civics and Government - Demonstrate an understanding of the origins and purposes of government, law, and the American political system

standards.text: Analyze the influences of ancient Greece, ancient Rome and the Judeo- Christian tradition on America’s constitutional republic.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Trace the principles underlying America’s founding ideas on law and government.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Trace the impact that the Magna Carta, Mayflower Compact, English Bill of Rights and Thomas Paine’s Common Sense had on colonists’ views of government.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Analyze how Enlightenment ideas, including Montesquieu’s view of separation of powers and John Locke’s theories related to natural law and Locke’s social contract, influenced the Founding.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe how British policies and responses to colonial concerns led to the writing of the Declaration of Independence.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Analyze the ideas and grievances set forth in the Declaration of Independence.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain how the weaknesses of the Articles of Confederation led to the writing of the U.S. Constitution.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the purpose of the Preamble to the U.S. Constitution.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe how the U.S. Constitution limits the powers of government through separation of powers, checks and balances, individual rights, rule of law, and due process of law.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Compare the viewpoints of the Federalists and the Anti-Federalists regarding ratification of the U.S. Constitution and including a bill of rights.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Define the rule of law and recognize its influence on the development of legal, political, and governmental systems in the United States.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Civics and Government - Evaluate the roles, rights, and responsibilities of United States citizens, and determine methods of active participation in society, government, and the political system

standards.text: Define the term “citizen,” and explain the constitutional means of becoming a U.S. citizen.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Differentiate between obligations and responsibilities of U.S. citizenship and evaluate their impact on society.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify and apply the rights contained in the Bill of Rights and other amendments to the U.S. Constitution.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain how the U.S. Constitution and the Bill of Rights safeguard individual rights.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe the trial process and the role of juries in the administration of justice at the state and federal levels.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Examine the election and voting process at the local, state, and national levels.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify the constitutional qualifications required to hold local, state, and national offices.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Examine the impact of media, individuals, and interest groups on monitoring and influencing government.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Analyze media and political communications and identify examples of bias, symbolism, and propaganda.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the process for citizens to address a state or local problem by researching public policy alternatives, identifying appropriate government agencies to address the issue, and determining a course of action.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Civics and Government - Demonstrate an understanding of the principles, functions, and organization of government

standards.text: Analyze the advantages of the United States’ constitutional republic over other forms of government in safeguarding liberty, freedom, and a representative government.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the advantages of a federal system of government over other systems in balancing local sovereignty with national unity and protecting against authoritarianism.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe the structure and function of the three branches of government established in the U.S. Constitution.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the relationship between state and national governments as written in Article IV of the U.S. Constitution and the 10th Amendment.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the amendment process outlined in Article V of the U.S. Constitution.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Analyze how the 13th, 14th, 15th, 19th, 24th, and 26th Amendments broadened participation in the political process.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the structure, functions, and processes of the legislative branch of government.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the structure, functions, and processes of the executive branch of government.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the structure, functions, and processes of the judicial branch of government.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify sources and types of law.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Analyze the effects of landmark Supreme Court decisions on law, liberty, and the interpretation of the U.S. Constitution.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Compare the U.S. and Florida constitutions.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain government obligations to its citizens and the services provided at the local, state, and national levels.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the purpose and function of the Electoral College in electing the President of the United States.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Analyze the advantages of capitalism and the free market in the United States over government-controlled economic systems (e.g., socialism and communism) in regard to economic freedom and raising the standard of living for citizens.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Civics and Government - Demonstrate an understanding of contemporary issues in world affairs, and evaluate the role and impact of United States foreign policy

standards.text: Explain the relationship between U.S. foreign and domestic policy.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe the United States’ and citizen participation in international organizations.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe examples of the United States’ actions and reactions in international conflicts.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the significance of September 11, 2001.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Economics - Understand the fundamental concepts relevant to the development of a market economy

standards.text: Explain how the principles of a market and mixed economy helped to develop the United States into a democratic nation.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Discuss the importance of borrowing and lending in the United States, the government's role in controlling financial institutions and list the advantages and disadvantages of using credit.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Review the concepts of supply and demand, choice, scarcity, and opportunity cost as they relate to the development of the mixed market economy in the United States.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Discuss the function of financial institutions in the development of a market economy.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Assess how profits, incentives, and competition motivate individuals, households, and businesses in a free market economy.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Compare the national budget process to the personal budget process.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Economics - Understand the fundamental concepts relevant to the institutions, structure, and functions of a national economy

standards.text: Explain how federal, state, and local taxes support the economy as a function of the United States government.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe the banking system in the United States and its impact on the money supply.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify and describe United States laws and regulations adopted to promote economic competition.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify entrepreneurs from various gender, social, and ethnic backgrounds who started a business seeking to make a profit.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain how economic institutions impact the national economy.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Economics - Understand the fundamental concepts and interrelationships of the United States economy in the international marketplace

standards.text: Explain how international trade requires a system for exchanging currency between and among nations.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Assess how the changing value of currency affects trade of goods and services between nations.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Compare and contrast a single resource economy with a diversified economy.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Compare and contrast the standard of living in various countries today to that of the United States using gross domestic product (GDP) per capita as an indicator.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geography - Understand how to use maps and other geographic representations, tools, and technology to report information

standards.text: Locate the fifty states and their capital cities in addition to the nation’s capital on a map.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Locate on a world map the territories and protectorates of the United States of America.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Interpret maps to identify geopolitical divisions and boundaries of places in North America.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geography - Understand physical and cultural characteristics of places

standards.text: Locate major cultural landmarks that are emblematic of the United States.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Locate major physical landmarks that are emblematic of the United States.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain how major physical characteristics, natural resources, climate, and absolute and relative location have influenced settlement, economies, and inter-governmental relations in North America.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe current major cultural regions of North America.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geography - Understand the relationships between the Earth’s ecosystems and the populations that dwell within them

standards.text: Use maps to describe the location, abundance, and variety of natural resources in North America.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geography - Understand the characteristics, distribution, and migration of human populations

standards.text: Use geographic terms and tools to explain cultural diffusion throughout North America.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Use maps and other geographic tools to examine the importance of demographics within political divisions of the United States.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geography - Understand how human actions can impact the environment

standards.text: Use a choropleth or other map to geographically represent current information about issues of conservation or ecology in the local community.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Geography - Understand how to apply geography to interpret the past and present, and plan for the future

standards.text: Use Geographic Information Systems (GIS) or other technology to view maps of current information about the United States.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: History of Communism - Assess the effects of communist governments

standards.text: Assess the effects of communist governments on individual freedoms, political participation, and the economy.
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: African American History - Understand the causes, courses, and consequences of the slave trade in the colonies

standards.text: Identify Afro-Eurasian trade routes and methods prior to the development of the Atlantic slave trade.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe the contact of European explorers with systematic slave trading in Africa.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Examine the evolution of the labor force in the use of indentured servitude contracts.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe the history and evolution of slave codes.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Analyze slave revolts that happened in early colonial America and how political leaders reacted (e.g., 1712 revolt in New York City, Stono Rebellion [1739]).
standards.label: A

standards.text: Examine the service and sacrifice of African patriots during the Revolutionary Era (e.g., Crispus Attucks, Peter Salem, James Armistead Lafayette, 1st Rhode Island Regiment).
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: African American History - Analyze events that involved or affected Africans from the founding of the nation through Reconstruction

standards.text: Explain early congressional actions regarding the institution of slavery (i.e., Northwest Ordinance of 1787, Three-Fifths Compromise, Act Prohibiting Importation of Slaves of 1808).
standards.label: A

standards.text: Explain the effect of the cotton industry on the expansion of slavery due to Eli Whitney’s Cotton Gin.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Examine the various duties and trades performed by slaves (e.g., agricultural work, painting, carpentry, tailoring, domestic service, blacksmithing, transportation).
standards.label: A

standards.text: Examine the Underground Railroad and its importance to those seeking freedom.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Identify political figures who strove to abolish the institution of slavery (e.g., Thaddeus Stevens, Abraham Lincoln, Zachariah Chandler).
standards.label: A

standards.text: Evaluate various abolitionist movements that continuously pushed to end slavery.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Examine how the status of slaves, those who had escaped slavery and free blacks, affected their contributions to the Civil War effort.
standards.label: A

standards.text: Describe significant contributions made by key figures during Reconstruction (e.g., President Ulysses S. Grant, Secretary of War Edwin Stanton, Frederick Douglass, Lyman Trumbull).
standards.label: A

domains.domain_name: Holocaust Education - Foundations of Holocaust Education

standards.text: Examine the Holocaust as the planned and systematic state-sponsored persecution and murder of European Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators between 1933 and 1945.
standards.label: A

key_learning_outcomes.label: C
items: Students trace influences on the U.S. constitutional republic, the Declaration of Independence and Constitution, and limits on government power.
Students explain citizenship, the Bill of Rights, elections, the three branches, and U.S. foreign policy, including September 11, 2001.
Students describe the U.S. mixed market economy, taxes, banking, trade, and geography of the United States and North America.
Students assess effects of communist governments on freedom, political participation, and the economy.
The shared Grades 6-8 benchmarks stored in this file cover the slave trade and Africans through Reconstruction, and the Holocaust as state-sponsored persecution and murder of European Jews.

notes: Organization: by_grade for SS.7 codes (Civics and Government, Economics, Geography, History of Communism). Not a 9-12 course.

HOME FOR THE SHARED BAND: SS.68.AA and SS.68.HE (15 benchmarks) apply across grades 6-8, not to grade 7 only. Grade 6 omitted them. This grade-7 file is the single stored copy. Grade 8 must not duplicate SS.68.*. They are appended after the SS.7 benchmarks.

Benchmark statements extracted from the clean 2026 social studies standards DOCX incorporated by Rule 6A-1.09401 (Ref-19653). Benchmark clarifications are omitted from standard text. Printed pages: SS.7 on 60-73; SS.68 band on 47-49 of the DOCX converted to PDF.
Running headers that repeat SS.7.G.1 and SS.7.G.4 titles inside one paragraph are stored once.

Kept as printed, not corrected: SS.7.CG.1.1 has a space after the hyphen in “Judeo- Christian.” SS.7.E.1.2 uses a straight apostrophe in “government's”; other possessives in this grade use a curly apostrophe.
